summary: GPU slot erosion leading to steady P50 throughput ceiling in dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: BrightPages is observing a stable P50 throughput ceiling in their dedicated pool despite autoscaler adding GPU capacity. Impact: sustained lower throughput for production inference routes impacting response times for API customers. Environment: BrightPages dedicated pool (pool-id: bp-44), A100-80GB nodes, autoscale policy default-burst, reserved capacity 12 -> observed >20 GPUs allocated during spikes. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send 2500 concurrent short-stream requests (avg prompt 80 tokens) over 10 minutes to project route /v1/generate pinned to llama-2-70b. 2) Monitor pool GPU allocation and per-GPU queue depth dashboards. Observed behavior: Autoscaler increases node count, but P50 throughput plateaus and does not improve after additional GPUs are added; CPU and SM utilization on many GPUs remain low while a subset shows high inference queue depth and serialized kernel execution. Expected behavior: Throughput should increase proportionally when autoscaler adds capacity and requests can be scheduled across new GPUs. Logs & dashboards referenced: pool metrics, scheduler allocation logs, and kernel-queue traces attached in comments.
